summary: Iteration 12 - Google Calendar bidirectional sync integration tested. Backend: 10/10 pytest pass covering all new /api/calendar/google/* endpoints plus auth/tasks/local-calendar regression. Frontend: Calendar page loads with Google Calendar connection bar, 'Connect Google Calendar' button visible, Add Event modal opens/closes correctly, login + SPA nav via sidebar works (in-memory tokenStore). No critical issues found.

issues: Radix Dialog console warning: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby for DialogContent' (a11y, non-blocking)

passed_tests: GET /api/calendar/google/connect -> 200 authorization_url starts with https://accounts.google.com and includes client_id/redirect_uri/response_type/scope/state
Frontend: SPA nav via sidebar -> /dashboard/calendar loads (data-testid=calendar-page)
Frontend: google-calendar-bar visible with correct 'Connect to sync events with Google Calendar' message
Frontend: connect-google-btn visible with label 'Connect Google Calendar'
Frontend: add-event-button visible; modal opens with event-title-input; cancel closes modal
action_items: (Low prio) Add DialogDescription or aria-describedby to Add Event modal DialogContent to fix Radix a11y console warning
(Future) When a user actually connects Google Calendar in a real session, re-test /events, /sync/pull, /sync/push with valid tokens (cannot be tested here without real OAuth consent)
critical_code_review_comments: google_calendar.py: OAuth state stored in db.google_oauth_states but has no TTL/cleanup; consider expiring stale states (>10 min) to prevent unbounded growth.

google_calendar.py: create_google_event and delete_google_event call _get_google_creds(user_id) without passing request; fine since request is optional but inconsistent with get_google_events — acceptable.

google_calendar.py: sync_push iterates local events with google_event_id:{$exists: false} — OK, but there is no dedup guard if the same Google event was imported and then re-pushed; current code uses $exists check which handles this correctly.
CalendarPage.js: checkGoogleStatus has eslint-disable for exhaustive-deps; loadGoogleEvents is referenced but not in deps — acceptable since functions are stable, noted for awareness.

Redirect URI is built from request.base_url per-call — must exactly match the URI registered in Google Cloud Console; if behind proxy, ensure X-Forwarded-* headers are honored (FastAPI ProxyHeadersMiddleware). Not tested here.
seed_data_creation: None. test_disconnect is idempotent; no persistent test data created.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_12 validated Google Calendar OAuth connect/status/disconnect and the unconnected-state 400s for events/sync/pull/sync/push. Full OAuth round-trip with real Google tokens is NOT covered (requires human consent). To test push/pull success paths, a user must complete the OAuth consent in a real browser; then the google_tokens field in db.users enables service.events() calls. The backend gracefully handles expired tokens by clearing them and returning 401. Frontend uses in-memory tokenStore so use SPA link clicks (not page.goto) to navigate between authenticated pages.
